title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The lightbulb reads the column too
summary: Kotlin writes the fields of a data class on one line. The quick fix matched its finding on the line alone, so opening it on the second field offered to delete the first.

highlights.title: Delete the field you pointed at
highlights.description: A data class with two unread fields on one line now offers each field its own fix, with the right name in the title and the right text removed.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The unread field fix acts on the field under the cursor. On a data class written as one line, the first field of the line won every time, so the title named it and the deletion removed its text.

The same rule now serves the enum entry and class member fixes, which matched on the line alone as well. Nothing visible changes there: an enum written on one line offers no deletion at all, because the module declines to compute a safe extent for it.
Measured on a real Android project: 34 data classes and 4 enums are written with several names on one line.
